citation_round1: Fleischner, Mujuni, Paulusma, Szeider, 'Covering graphs with few complete bipartite subgraphs,' Theoretical Computer Science 410(21-23):2045-2053, 2009 (prelim. FSTTCS 2007, LNCS 4855): the Biclique Cover problem (cover every edge of G by at most k bicliques), parameterized by k, is fixed-parameter tractable.
citation_check_round2: On-point. Fleischner, Mujuni, Paulusma, Szeider, TCS 410(21-23):2045-2053, 2009 (prelim. FSTTCS 2007) explicitly prove Biclique Cover (cover every edge of G by at most k bicliques), parameterized by k, is FPT (kernel of at most 2^k vertices via signature identification). The same paper shows biclique vertex-cover/vertex-partition are NOT FPT unless P=NP, but the edge-cover version claimed here is FPT.
parameter: number of bicliques k (the biclique-cover number = solution size)

citation_round1: Fomin, Fraigniaud, Golovach, 'Parameterized Complexity of Broadcasting in Graphs,' WG 2023 (LNCS 14093) / arXiv:2306.01536 (full version in Theoretical Computer Science, 2024): because n <= 2^t, their 3^n n^O(1) algorithm yields an FPT algorithm parameterized by the number of rounds t with double-exponential dependence 2^{2^{O(t)}}; the double-exponential dependence is essentially tight under ETH (see 'Double Exponential Lower Bound for Telephone Broadcast,' arXiv:2403.03501, 2024, building on a Papadimitriou-Yannakakis construction).
citation_check_round2: Supported. Fomin, Fraigniaud, Golovach (WG 2023 / TCS 2024) give a 3^n n^O(1) algorithm for Telephone Broadcast; since broadcast time t satisfies n <= 2^t, this is FPT in t with double-exponential dependence. Tale, 'Double Exponential Lower Bound for Telephone Broadcast' (arXiv:2403.03501, 2024) explicitly parameterizes by t (=solution size), notes n<=2^t and a 2^{2^{O(t)}} n^O(1) brute force, and proves no 2^{2^{o(t)}} n^O(1) algorithm unless ETH fails (tight). Both cited works support the claim.
parameter: number of rounds t (the broadcast time = objective/solution value); not named explicitly, canonical parameter

citation_round1: Dreyfus & Wagner, 'The Steiner problem in graphs,' Networks 1:195-207, 1971 (the 3^k n^O(1) subset dynamic program, which applies to the rooted directed case); Guo, Niedermeier, Suchy, 'Parameterized Complexity of Arc-Weighted Directed Steiner Problems,' SIAM J. Discrete Mathematics 25(2):583-599, 2011: Directed Steiner Tree is FPT parameterized by the number of terminals (whereas Strongly Connected Steiner Subgraph and Directed Steiner Network are W[1]-hard for that parameter).
citation_check_round2: On-point. The Dreyfus-Wagner 3^k n^O(1) subset DP extends to the rooted directed case (standard, e.g. Cygan et al. textbook). Guo, Niedermeier, Suchy, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 25(2):583-599, 2011 explicitly classify Directed Steiner Tree as FPT parameterized by the number of terminals, while Strongly Connected Steiner Subgraph and Directed Steiner Network are W[1]-hard for that parameter.
parameter: number of terminals

citation_round1: Garey & Johnson, 'Computers and Intractability: A Guide to the Theory of NP-Completeness,' W.H. Freeman, 1979, problem [GT3] Domatic Number: deciding whether the domatic number of a graph is at least 3 is NP-complete; hence the problem is NP-hard already for the fixed constant d=3.
citation_check_round2: Supported. Garey & Johnson (1979), Domatic Number [GT3]: deciding whether V(G) can be partitioned into 3 dominating sets (domatic number >= 3) is NP-complete; hence NP-hard at the fixed constant d=3. This is exactly para-NP-hardness w.r.t. the target domatic number d.
parameter: the domatic number d (target number of disjoint dominating sets = solution value)

citation_round1: General (binary-encoded) Bin Packing is NP-hard already for k=2 bins because 2-bin packing is exactly the Partition problem (NP-complete; Karp 1972; Garey & Johnson 1979 [SP12]); 2D Bin Packing generalizes 1D (set all heights = 1), so it is NP-hard for the fixed constant k=2. Cf. Jansen, Kratsch, Marx, Schlotter, 'Bin packing with fixed number of bins revisited,' J. Comput. Syst. Sci. 79(1):39-49, 2013 (prelim. SWAT 2010), who additionally prove the unary variant is W[1]-hard parameterized by #bins.
citation_check_round2: Correct. Binary-encoded 2-bin (1D) packing is exactly Partition (NP-complete; Karp 1972; G&J [SP12]); 2D/geometric bin packing generalizes 1D (set heights=1), so it is NP-hard at the fixed constant k=2 bins. Jansen, Kratsch, Marx, Schlotter (JCSS 79(1):39-49, 2013) additionally prove the unary variant is W[1]-hard by #bins - a correct supplementary note.
parameter: number of bins k

citation_round1: Marx, 'Efficient Approximation Schemes for Geometric Problems?', ESA 2005 (LNCS 3669, pp. 448-459): deciding whether n given points in the plane can be covered by k unit disks is W[1]-hard parameterized by k (no f(k)*n^O(1) algorithm unless FPT=W[1]).
citation_check_round2: Supported. Marx, 'Efficient Approximation Schemes for Geometric Problems?', ESA 2005 (LNCS 3669:448-459) proves Max Independent Set W[1]-hard for unit disks AND unit squares, and geometric point-cover W[1]-hard. The paper's abstract phrases the covering theorem for unit squares, but recent literature (e.g. arXiv:2607.08183, 2026) explicitly attributes to Marx ESA 2005 the statement that no f(k)n^O(1) algorithm decides whether n points can be covered by k unit disks unless FPT=W[1], noting Marx's hardness applies to both disks and squares. Citation holds at R20.
parameter: k = number of unit disks used to cover all points (free centres)

citation_round1: Kobayashi & Otachi, 'Parameterized Complexity of Graph Burning', IPEC 2020 (LIPIcs vol. 180, art. 21); journal version Algorithmica 84(8):2379-2393 (2022): Graph Burning is W[2]-complete parameterized by the burning number k.
citation_check_round2: Exact. Kobayashi & Otachi, 'Parameterized Complexity of Graph Burning', IPEC 2020 (LIPIcs 180, art. 21); journal version Algorithmica 84(8):2379-2393 (2022) prove Graph Burning is W[2]-complete parameterized by the burning number k. W[2]-complete falls within the claimed 'W[2]+' bucket.
parameter: k = burning number b(G) (target number of rounds / fire sources)

citation_round1: van Bevern, Mnich, Niedermeier, Weller, 'Interval scheduling and colorful independent sets', Journal of Scheduling 18(5):449-469 (2015) (prelim. ISAAC 2012, LNCS 7676): Job Interval Selection (Independent Set on strip graphs, generalized to 2-union graphs) is fixed-parameter tractable w.r.t. the parameter k = number of selected intervals/jobs.
citation_check_round2: On-point. van Bevern, Mnich, Niedermeier, Weller, 'Interval scheduling and colorful independent sets', J. Scheduling 18(5):449-469, 2015 (prelim. ISAAC 2012) prove Job Interval Selection (= Independent Set on strip graphs) is FPT parameterized by k = number of selected jobs, extending Halldorsson-Karlsson's algorithm. The paper's dichotomy shows Independent Set on the more general 2-union graphs is W[1]-hard, but JISP itself is FPT - the claim targets the FPT problem correctly.
parameter: k = number of selected/scheduled jobs (solution size / objective)

citation_round1: W[2]-hard via the standard reduction from Dominating Set, which is W[2]-complete (Downey & Fellows, 1995, SIAM J. Comput.); stated explicitly for k-center by Feldmann, 'Fixed-Parameter Approximations for k-Center Problems in Low Highway Dimension Graphs', ICALP 2015 / Algorithmica 81(3):1031-1052 (2019): k-center is W[2]-hard for parameter k.
citation_check_round2: Feldmann (ICALP 2015 / Algorithmica 81(3):1031-1052, 2019) states k-center is W[2]-hard for parameter k; hardness stems from Dominating Set (W[2]-complete, Downey-Fellows). Even (2-eps)-approximation is W[2]-hard for k. Citation on-point.
parameter: k = number of centers/radius-r balls

citation_round1: Color-coding (Alon, Yuster, Zwick, 'Color-Coding', J. ACM 42(4):844-856, 1995) finds a minimum-weight k-vertex tree/bounded-treewidth subgraph in 2^O(k)*poly(n); explicit min-weight k-tree bound Õ(2^k*poly(k)*M*n^3) in Hassidim, Keller, Lewenstein, Roditty, 'Finding the Minimum-Weight k-Path', WADS 2013 (LNCS 8037).
citation_check_round2: Alon-Yuster-Zwick color-coding (J.ACM 1995) finds a min-weight k-vertex tree (treewidth-1 pattern) in 2^O(k)*poly(n); weighted extension is standard (Cygan et al. textbook). Note: the Hassidim-Keller-Lewenstein-Roditty (WADS 2013) citation is specifically min-weight k-PATH, not k-tree, so mildly mislabeled, but AYZ fully supports the FPT value.
parameter: k = target number of vertices the tree must span

citation_round1: Bonnet, Paschos, Sikora, 'Parameterized exact and approximation algorithms for maximum k-set cover and related satisfiability problems', RAIRO-ITA 50(3):227-240 (2016): Max k-Set Cover (= Maximum Coverage) is W[2]-hard parameterized by k (the number of sets) and FPT parameterized by p (elements covered). Also folklore from Set Cover W[2]-completeness (Downey & Fellows, 1995).
citation_check_round2: Bonnet-Paschos-Sikora (RAIRO-ITA 50(3):227-240, 2016) explicitly prove Max k-Set Cover is W[2]-hard parameterized by k (number of sets) and FPT parameterized by p (elements covered). Also follows from Set Cover W[2]-completeness (setting coverage target = |U|). Citation exact and on-point.
parameter: k = budget (number of sets selected)

citation_round1: Cai, 'Parameterized Complexity of Cardinality Constrained Optimization Problems,' The Computer Journal 51(1):102-121, 2008 — Densest-k-Subgraph is W[1]-hard parameterized by k; metric max-sum p-dispersion equals Densest-p-Subgraph plus an additive constant under the standard {1,2}-metric (edge=2, non-edge=1), a parameter-preserving reduction with p=k (equivalently the classical Clique reduction, Clique being W[1]-complete, Downey & Fellows 1995).
citation_check_round2: Cai (Computer Journal 51(1):102-121, 2008) proves Densest-k-Subgraph / Maximum-k-Edge-Subgraph is W[1]-hard by reduction from k-Clique. The {1,2}-metric identity sum-dispersion(S) = C(p,2) + e(S) is a valid parameter-preserving (p=k) reduction. Citation supports the hardness source.
parameter: p, the cardinality of the selected subset

citation_round1: K. Jansen, 'The optimum cost chromatic partition problem,' CIAC 1997 (LNCS 1203, pp. 25-36): DP solves vertex chromatic sum on treewidth-k graphs in O(n*(log n)^(k+1)) time; this is FPT-bounded because an optimal sum coloring uses O(tw*log n) colors (Grundy-number bound), giving f(tw)*poly(n).
citation_check_round2: Jansen (CIAC 1997, LNCS 1203, pp.25-36) gives an O(n*(log n)^(tw+1)) algorithm for OCCP on partial k-trees; vertex chromatic sum (min sum coloring) is the special case cost(i)=i. (log n)^(f(tw)) is FPT-bounded, and optimal sum colorings use O(tw*log n) colors (Grundy bound), so the algorithm is FPT. Citation supports the value.
parameter: treewidth

citation_round1: Chandra & Wong, 'Worst-case analysis of a placement algorithm related to storage allocation,' SIAM J. Comput. 4(3):249-263, 1975, define partitioning n numbers into m parts minimizing the sum of squared part-sums and note NP-completeness; the m=2 case is NP-hard by reduction from PARTITION (the 2-machine sum-of-squares optimum is the most balanced partition), so the problem is para-NP-hard parameterized by m.
citation_check_round2: Value correct: at m=2, minimizing S^2+(T-S)^2 is minimized by the most balanced split, and achieving T^2/2 <=> PARTITION yes-instance, so NP-hard at fixed m=2 => para-NP-hard by m. Chandra-Wong (SIAM J.Comput. 4(3):249-263, 1975) defines the problem but is a heuristic worst-case-ratio paper and does not itself prove NP-completeness; the clean citation is Garey & Johnson (MINIMUM SUM OF SQUARES, NP-complete) plus the folklore PARTITION reduction.
parameter: number of bins/machines m (natural parameter; not explicitly named in task)

citation_round1: M. Hoffmann & Y. Okamoto, 'The minimum weight triangulation problem with few inner points,' IWPEC 2004 (LNCS 3162, pp. 200-212), journal version Comput. Geom. 34(3):149-158, 2006: MWT of a point set with k interior points computable in O(6^k * n^5 * log n) time (improved to 2^{O(sqrt(k) log k)}*poly(n) by Knauer & Spillner, WG 2006, LNCS 4271).
citation_check_round2: Hoffmann & Okamoto (IWPEC 2004, LNCS 3162; Comput. Geom. 34(3):149-158, 2006) give an exact O(6^k * n^5 * log n) algorithm parameterized by the number k of interior points; Knauer-Spillner (2005/2006) improve to 2^{O(sqrt(k) log k)}*poly(n). Citation exact and on-point.
parameter: number of inner (interior) points k

citation_round1: For d=1 the problem is the classical 0/1 Knapsack, NP-complete (Karp, 'Reducibility Among Combinatorial Problems,' 1972; Garey & Johnson 1979, MP9); NP-hardness at the fixed value d=1 yields para-NP-hardness parameterized by d. (Refinement: the unary/pseudo-poly variant, multidimensional subset sum, is W[1]-hard parameterized by the number of dimensions even with unary weights, via a Multicolored-Clique reduction.)
citation_check_round2: Correct and on-point. At d=1 the problem is exactly 0/1 Knapsack, which is NP-complete (Karp 1972 lists Knapsack among the 21; Garey & Johnson 1979 [MP9] KNAPSACK). NP-hardness at the fixed constant d=1 yields para-NP-hardness parameterized by d. The refinement (unary multidimensional subset sum W[1]-hard by number of dimensions via multicolored-clique) is also a genuine result and correctly stated, though it concerns a different variant.
parameter: dimension d (number of weight dimensions / packing constraints)

citation_round1: SAT (hence 3-SAT, planar 3-SAT, and MAX-SAT) is FPT parameterized by incidence treewidth: Samer & Szeider, 'Algorithms for propositional model counting,' J. Discrete Algorithms 8(1):50-64, 2010 (conf. 2006), time O(4^{tw}*poly); more generally Courcelle's theorem (1990) gives FPT for MSO properties on bounded-treewidth structures.
citation_check_round2: Correct. Samer & Szeider (J. Discrete Algorithms 8(1):50-64, 2010) establish that #SAT is FPT parameterized by incidence treewidth (O(4^{tw} poly), later improved to 2^{tw} by Slivovsky-Szeider); decision SAT/3-SAT (hence planar 3-SAT) is at least as easy, and Courcelle's theorem gives FPT for the MSO-expressible satisfiability property on the bounded-treewidth incidence structure. Note: the Boolean-CSP W[1]-hardness caveat applies only to arbitrary-relation CSP, not bounded-arity 3-SAT.
parameter: treewidth (of the variable-clause incidence graph)

citation_round1: Jiang, Zhang & Zhu, 'Weak Kernels', ECCC TR10-005 (2010, rev. 2012): Sorting an UNSIGNED permutation by the minimum number of reversals admits a weak kernel of size 4k, giving the first FPT algorithm, running in O(2^{2k} n + n log n) time, parameterized by the reversal distance k.
citation_check_round2: Exact match verified against the primary source. ECCC TR10-005 (rev. 5, 2012), Theorem 2: 'Sorting with Minimum Unsigned Reversals has a weak kernel of size 4k, hence can be solved in O(2^{2k} n + n log n) time.' The abstract states this is 'the first FPT algorithm for the famous Sorting by Minimum Unsigned Reversals problem.' Kernel size 4k, running time, and parameterization by reversal distance k all match verbatim.
parameter: reversal distance k (number of reversals)

citation_round1: Feldmann & Marx, 'The Complexity Landscape of Fixed-Parameter Directed Steiner Network Problems', ICALP 2016 / ACM Trans. Comput. Theory 15(3-4):1-45 (2023): the partition of terminals into solution trees 'implies the fixed-parameter tractability of Steiner Forest parameterized by k=|R|' (undirected), solving each class via Dreyfus & Wagner (1971) Steiner Tree in 3^{|R|} poly(n).
citation_check_round2: Correct and on-point. Feldmann & Marx (ICALP 2016 / ACM ToCT 2023) state the observation on partitioning terminals into solution trees 'implies the fixed-parameter tractability of Steiner Forest parameterized by the number of terminals' (quote confirmed near-verbatim). The result is standard folklore: guess the partition of the 2k terminals (Bell number, a function of k) consistent with the demand pairs, then solve each class by Dreyfus-Wagner Steiner Tree in 3^{|R|} poly(n). |R| = 2 x pairs, so FPT by pairs = FPT by |R|.
parameter: number of terminal pairs (equivalently number of terminals |R| = 2 x pairs)

citation_round1: Ashok, Kolay, Meesum & Saurabh, 'Parameterized complexity of Strip Packing and Minimum Volume Packing', Theoretical Computer Science 661:56-64 (2017): 2D Strip Packing is W[1]-hard parameterized by the height of the optimal packing (and FPT when parameterized by height plus the maximum item dimension).
citation_check_round2: Correct. Ashok, Kolay, Meesum & Saurabh, 'Parameterized complexity of Strip Packing and Minimum Volume Packing', Theoretical Computer Science 661:56-64, 2017 (DOI 10.1016/j.tcs.2016.11.034) prove 2D Strip Packing is W[1]-hard parameterized by the height of the optimal packing (confirmed via the article abstract, Wikipedia, and search). The paper additionally gives an FPT algorithm for a restricted case, consistent with the 'height plus max item dimension' refinement.
parameter: natural parameter = height of the (optimal) packing, the minimization objective

citation_round1: R||Cmax generalizes P2||Cmax (set p_1j=p_2j=p_j); minimizing makespan on 2 identical machines is NP-complete by reduction from PARTITION (Garey & Johnson, 'Computers and Intractability', W.H. Freeman, 1979; classified in Lenstra, Rinnooy Kan & Brucker, 'Complexity of machine scheduling problems', Annals of Discrete Mathematics 1:343-362, 1977). NP-hard at the fixed constant m=2, therefore para-NP-hard parameterized by the number of machines m.
citation_check_round2: Correct and on-point. R||Cmax generalizes P2||Cmax (set p_ij = p_j), and minimizing makespan on 2 identical machines is NP-complete by reduction from PARTITION (Garey & Johnson 1979, the textbook example; classified in Lenstra, Rinnooy Kan & Brucker 1977). NP-hard at the fixed constant m=2, therefore para-NP-hard parameterized by m.
parameter: number of machines m

citation_round1: Minimizing total weighted completion time on 2 identical parallel machines (P2||sum w_j C_j) is NP-hard: Bruno, Coffman & Sethi, 'Scheduling independent tasks to reduce mean finishing time', Communications of the ACM 17(7):382-387, 1974 (also classified in Lenstra, Rinnooy Kan & Brucker, Annals of Discrete Mathematics 1:343-362, 1977). NP-hard at the fixed constant m=2, therefore para-NP-hard parameterized by the number of machines m.
citation_check_round2: Correct and on-point. P2||sum w_j C_j is NP-hard (Bruno, Coffman & Sethi, CACM 17(7):382-387, 1974 - confirmed by search: 'the special case of two identical machines is NP-hard in the ordinary sense'; also in Lenstra, Rinnooy Kan & Brucker 1977). Unweighted P||sum C_j is polynomial (SPT), but the weighted 2-machine case is NP-hard. NP-hard at the fixed constant m=2, therefore para-NP-hard parameterized by m.
parameter: number of machines m
